cohort: 10,646 nonanomalous, SGA, late preterm (≥34 and <37 weeks) singleton and twin pregnancies from a cohort of 1.85 million pregnancies
finding: Compared to singleton pregnancies, late preterm SGA twin pregnancies had a higher risk of cesarean delivery, postpartum hemorrhage, and maternal transfusion but a lower risk of neonatal death and intrauterine fetal demise.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery rates were higher in SGA <10th percentile twin pregnancies compared to singleton pregnancies (aOR 3.40; 95% CI 3.01-3.90; p < .001).
